correctness.rationale: For any \(p\ge2\) and \(n\ge6p-3\), exact source theorem guarantees reduced homology only in degree \(n-4\) and gives beta. Complement-of-facets reasoning identifies dual faces with vertex subsets having at most one nonneighbor apiece. For a rotation of order \(m\ge3\), choosing the orbit vertices at distances >=\(n/3\) (or \(n/4\) for \(m=4\)) produces two nonneighbors and excludes all nonempty fixed simplices. The half-turn fixes exactly \(n/2\) antipodal edges, each with signed Lefschetz contribution +1. Connectedness and cohomology concentration convert these alternating traces to the full \(H^1\) character. Equivariant Alexander duality twists by ambient permutation sign. Rational representation decomposition follows from exact cyclic characters. The independent standalone program reconstructed 6426 dual faces, checked 186 nonidentity rotation traces, 12 exact binary \(H_1\) ranks, and 42 original-cut action traces; finite tests are not the all-parameter proof.

value.rationale: The question is structurally motivated by the new shellability classification of the graph family and its natural cyclic graph automorphism group. Classifying the complete rational homology representation, rather than only its dimension, is new symmetry information for infinitely many n,p: a half-turn has a distinguished character and forces an induced nontrivial subgroup summand precisely at even n. This cannot be read from the published sphere multiplicity, is not an arbitrary slice, and does not require speculative downstream utility.
